final_message:
The scope contracts are written and Board Review has been crossed, so the plan stops here, before Build. The run is `envlint-20261109T033912Z-c549b0b1`. Because it was unattended, the `ci` answer set crossed every gate and nobody reviewed them. All five gates (Intake & Config, Orient Review, Wiring Review, Board Review, and the run opening) have `ok` rows in `.shapeup/envlint/gates.jsonl`. The hook ledger has no denials.

**What exists now:**
- **Requirements:** `shapeup/envlint/requirements.md` breaks the pitch into 30 single-clause requirements, REQ-1 to REQ-30. Every one is graded by at least one task's acceptance criteria and claimed by at least one scope. I checked this by reading the files back.
- **Spec:** `shapeup/envlint/spec/` holds three use cases: parse the `.env` text, check it against the schema, and the `envlint` command itself. Each has its list of tests to grade against.
- **Board:** four tasks in `.shapeup/envlint/tasks/` (this machine only). The estimate is 8.5 hours, which fits the one build round the pitch allows.
- **Wiring map:** `shapeup/envlint/wiring-map.md` shows both modules plugging into `bin/envlint.mjs`.
- **Scopes:** in `shapeup/envlint/scopes/`. No file appears in two scopes, so parsing and rules can build at the same time and the CLI builds after them.

| Scope | Files | Depends on | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| parsing | `src/parse.mjs`, `test/parse.test.mjs` | — | `node --test test/parse.test.mjs` |
| rules | `src/rules.mjs`, `test/rules.test.mjs` | — | `node --test test/rules.test.mjs` |
| cli | `bin/envlint.mjs`, `test/cli.test.mjs`, `test/boundaries.test.mjs` | parsing, rules | `node --test test/cli.test.mjs test/boundaries.test.mjs` |

**Things to review before Build, since no one did:**
1. **Seven spec decisions the pitch left open.** I took them from the Scout's recommendations; they are listed as SD-1 to SD-7 in `spec/_index.md`:
   - parsed pairs are `{key, value, line}`, and with duplicate keys the last one wins;
   - an empty value counts as present for `required`;
   - `int` is `-?[0-9]+`, `bool` is exactly `true` or `false`, and `url` must be `http` or `https`;
   - exit codes are 0 for clean, 1 for findings, 2 for usage, read or schema errors;
   - a file with no assignments prints a notice and the rules still run;
   - keys not in the schema are ignored;
   - quoting is kept minimal, with no escape handling.

   Rejecting any of these now only means re-planning; after Build it means rework.
